top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a mature, experimentally reproduced achievement (Sr, Yb, Hg; accuracy moved from 1e-15 to about 1e-18) whose new content, magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms, is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes. The two-person allocation to Katori and Ye with the citation 'for the invention and development of the optical lattice clock' is defensible and narrowly scoped, and every member supports it. An award is preferable to no award.
